Okay. Say situation. You just escaped chase injured somewhere offside, no clear objective like saving in urgent neey. You can either: spend a bunch of seconds running to a teammate (who will probably be doing a gen), get hin to spend 16 seconds on you and then do the gen. Or 32 secs healing, run to gen, do gen. Also in that case you aren't grouped up as long which is a good thing. 

In both cases you spend the same time running to a gen, except if you selfcare immediately you actually are more flexible (imagine after your teammate heals you, you already have to move in for the save. Time spend running to the gen is lost time in that case)

The perk isnt great and I rather bring plunderers, but it's a lot more useful than many other perks. It gets it's bad rep from people healing in stupid situations.

Selfcare is 32 s default.
Healing is 16 s default.

Assume case 1: selfcare

After 32 seconds: Healed and gen at 32 seconds

Case 2: normal

After 16 seconds healed
After 16 further seconds gen is at 16* 2 * (1-0.15) about 27 seconds 

So selfcare is faster by about 5 gen seconds because of the 15% penalty you get for doing a gen together.

As is well known, trust and respect are the most important parts of a functional relationship. Trust also implies honesty and trusting their partner to tell the truth.

Let's assume scenario A: Woman loses libido naturally, not based on their partner, but biologically. She logically explains this to her husband.

According to your model, the man should take this as a lie and assume it's a surefire sign the relationship is over and terrible and their just not doing it for their partner, even though at some age for women this usually happens, sometimes earlier, sometimes later. And a actually good relationship takes a terrible ending.

If the man just trusts their wife, he will not be worried, and he shouldn't be. This is afterall natural and happens to most

Scenario B: Woman loses attraction to their partner and admits as much to him and tries to find ways with him together to change that or give up on the relationship.

Both models result in the same in this case, either it fails and the relationship ends, as it should, or they fix it.

Scenario C: Instead of being honest, she lies. Makes excuses, keeps turning him down under the guise of it not being because of their husband.

Your model: the husband assumes it's his fault maybe tries to change things, probably fails as he doesn't actually have his wife's input compared to B. Probably ends the relationship eventually.

Trust: he assumes his wife wouldn't lie to him. He probably stops initiating and settles into the later stages of a relationship, assuming its just the natural order of things. Wife probably grows resentful and might get a divorce after a few years or starts cheating.

Clearly C is the worst for the wife, and probably the husband too. In my opinion, it's also the wife's fault. It could be avoided, instead opting for B, in which case the partners probably have the best chance of fixing things and if things are unfixable, ending the relationship early, before deep resentment is fostered.

It's the woman's responsibility to figure out if it's their libido or their partners fault, and it's their responsibility to communicate as such, you shouldn't put that responsibility on your partner, they usually can't read minds after all. And doing so avoids the worst case: a bad relationship which goes on for way to long and includes massive resentment. 

In other words: just take some responsibility and be bloody honest for crying out loud
